subject: Evaluation plan slippage — rebaseline request & escalation
messages:
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@luminar.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation cadence — risk of slipping past May 14 close

Hi Michael / Lauren,

Quick note from the Luminar evaluation team: the internal infra team just pushed our performance test window out by two weeks due to a data retention legal check. That puts our planned production cutover (and the payment milestone) at risk of slipping beyond the May 14 target we agreed on in the MAP.

We want to avoid a hard stop on the PO, so can you confirm what minimum deliverables you need from us to preserve the May 14 date? If not possible, what would a safe rebaseline look like from your side (impact to cost / committed capacity)?

Also looping procurement (procurement@luminar.ai) since contracts may need a short amendment.

Thanks,
Jordan Hayes
Head of Platform Integrations
Luminar.ai

Attachment: evaluation-schedule-notice.txt (text)
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@luminar.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation cadence — risk of slipping past May 14 close

Jordan —

Thanks for the heads up. Short answer: we can preserve May 14 for a trimmed scope, but it requires an abbreviated evaluation (focused load window + sampling queries) and a quick sign-off process on the privacy checklist.

What I propose:
- We prepare a condensed MAP v2 that lists MUST-HAVE acceptance criteria (performance P95, KV cache hit baseline, and data residency check) and OPTIONAL follow-ups post-close.
- Redwood will reserve dedicated slots the week of May 10 for final validation (no extra charge if within the original committed hours).
- If Luminar cannot meet the condensed gate, we offer a single-week paid extension to the Dedicated pool at a discounted rate (we can propose details internally).

Lauren — can you draft a condensed MAP and call out what would trigger the paid extension vs. preserved commitment? Ben / Neha FYI for pricing/contract implications.

I'll aim to get an update to you by EOD Monday (Apr 12).

—Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: draft condensed MAP v2 for Luminar (internal review)

Team — draft condensed MAP attached. Key points I highlighted:
- Acceptance gate reduced to three focused tests (functional smoke, 30-min sustained qps, and data residency verification).
- Any failure on data residency automatically pauses the May 14 close and requires SOC2 evidence / encryption proofs (we should expect procurement asks).
- Pricing fallback: 1-week Dedicated extension at 40% off list, or maintain original price if Luminar can meet the condensed gate.

Ben: we need an OK on the 40% concession for the extension (this is time-limited offer).
Neha: if procurement asks for contract amendment language (SOW addendum), can you draft a short clause that allows a one-time date amendment without re-running procurement?

Attachments: luminar_map_v2.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: draft condensed MAP v2 for Luminar (internal review)

Lauren — I can approve the one-week 40% off extension as a standard concession for deals at this stage (RDW-8743 qualifies). Two quick notes:
1) Add a hard cap on token usage during the reserved validation slots — we should limit excess consumption (e.g., 10M tokens/week) to avoid open-ended cost.
2) Include an auto-fallback in the MAP: if the condensed gate fails, Redwood will revert to a compatibility model with slightly higher latency but guaranteed throughput so Luminar's pilot can continue while infrastructure/legal is remediated.

Neha — the procurement clause should be a short amendment with: affected milestone date, statement of no other changes, and signature from both parties. No pricing changes beyond the agreed concession. If you share a template I can flag client objections.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Evaluation cadence — risk of slipping past May 14 close

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick context. Attached is Condensed MAP v2 (luminar_map_v2.xlsx) with explicit acceptance gates and the two optional mitigations: 1) one-week dedicated extension at 40% off, capped at 10M tokens; 2) fallback model option to keep pilot running.

If Luminar can commit to the condensed gates and sign the short milestone amendment today, Redwood will hold the May 14 close and the reserved validation slots the week of May 10. If not, we recommend rebaseline to May 28 to accommodate the legal/data checks.

Please confirm which path you want to take. I can get the amendment drafted (no other contract changes) once procurement confirms.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
